title: Steering Away from Memorization: Reachability-Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Text-to-Image Diffusion
claim: Unconstrained sampling trajectories fall into an attractive failure region; steering the trajectory around that region avoids the failure while staying faithful.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right trajectories in a latent-space blob, with side image thumbnails
description: A large central panel labeled 'Diffusion Latent Space X' contains a pale red blob, the 'Attraction Basin of Memorization (modeled as BRT)'. A darker red ellipse inside it, in the upper right, is labeled 'Memorized Outputs'. A solid black curve starts at the initial noise point x_T on the left, passes through the basin and ends in the memorized region. A dashed green curve, labeled π_φ, starts at the same point and loops under the basin to a final latent x_0. The text 'Reachability-Aware Diffusion Steering (RADS)' sits at lower left. At the far left, a gray caption box and a memorized training sample image are stacked. On the right, two dotted lines link the trajectory endpoints to game-art thumbnails: the baseline image, labeled in red, nearly copies the training sample, and the RADS image, labeled in green, differs from it. The eye goes first to the red basin and the contrasting black and green paths.

abstract: Text-to-image diffusion models are susceptible to memorization, revealing a fundamental failure to generalize beyond the training set. Current mitigation approaches often sacrifice image quality or prompt alignment to reduce memorization. To address this, we propose Reachability-Aware Diffusion Steering (RADS), an offline-trained, sampling-time control framework that mitigates memorization while maintaining generation fidelity. RADS models the diffusion denoising process as a dynamical system and learns a policy-conditioned reachability value function that estimates future memorization risk along the denoising trajectory. This motivates a constrained reinforcement learning (RL) formulation, where a policy learns to steer the trajectory away from memorization via perturbations in the caption embedding space. Empirical evaluations show that RADS achieves a stronger empirical Pareto frontier between generation diversity (SSCD), quality (FID), and alignment (CLIP) compared to state-of-the-art inference-time baselines. Crucially, RADS applies the learned controller during sampling time, separating memorization mitigation from the pretrained model. Our website is available at: https://s-karnik.github.io/rads-memorization-project-page/.
